question: Superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction syndrome, characterised by facial oedema, distended neck veins, and headache worse on bending forward, most commonly results from a malignant anterior or middle mediastinal mass compressing or invading the SVC.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. SVC syndrome is overwhelmingly malignant in aetiology (lung cancer and lymphoma account for most cases) and results from tumour in the anterior or middle mediastinum compressing the SVC, which has thin walls and low intraluminal pressure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SVC obstruction syndrome is caused by compression or thrombosis of the SVC. In over 90% of cases the aetiology is malignant — most commonly lung cancer or lymphoma in the mediastinum. Facial oedema, venous distension, and postural headache are the classic features.
